sentences.text:
This Land Acquisition Appeal Having Been Finally
 Heard On 12.03.2025, The Court On The Same Day Delivered
 The Following:
Easwaran S., J.
The appeal arises out of the judgment and decree dated 30.11.2015 in L.A.R.No.106 of 2012 on the files of the II nd Additional Sub Court, Thiruvananthapuram.

entities.text: II nd Additional Sub Court, Thiruvananthapuram
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The brief facts necessary for disposal of this appeal are as follows:
An extent of 01.60 Ares of land in Sy.No.456/7 of Cheruvakkal Village in Thiruvananthapuram Taluk was acquired for the purpose of widening of Pattom-Medical College-Kochulloor Road.
Section 4(1) Notification was issued on 21.12.2005, and the award was passed on 19.07.2007.
The Land Acquisition Officer fixed the land value at Rs.2,39,248/- per Are, and a total compensation of Rs.7,05,739/- was granted to the claimant.
Dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation, the claimant sought reference under Section 18 of the erstwhile Land Acquisition Act.
In support of her claim, the claimant relied on the judgment dated 23.01.2013 in L.A.R.No.989 of 2009 in respect of the same acquisition.
The Reference Court, relying on the aforesaid document, fixed the land value at Rs.24,17,100/- per Are.

L.A.A.No.209/2018 :: 3 ::
 2025:KER:21099 Dissatisfied with the land value fixed by the Reference Court, the claimant has preferred the present appeal.

sentences.text:
2 3. Heard Sri.C.S.Manu, the learned counsel appearing for the appellant, Sri.T.K.Shajahan, the learned senior Government Pleader appearing for the 1st respondent State and Smt.Smitha S. Pillai,
the learned counsel appearing for the 2nd respondent.

4. On a consideration of the rival submissions made across the bar, we find that the Reference Court was not justified in fixing the land value at Rs.24,17,100/- especially since the Notification in the present case was issued on 21.12.2005, whereas the judgment in L.A.R.No.989 of 2019 pertains to the Notification dated 24.12.2004.

The claimant was thus entitled for an escalation at the rate of 10% going by the decision of the Supreme Court in General Manager, Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Limited v. Rameshbhai Jivanbhai Patel and Another - [(2008) 14 SCC 745].

entities.text: General Manager, Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Limited v. Rameshbhai Jivanbhai Patel and Another - [(2008) 14 SCC 745]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore,
we find that the appellant/claimant is entitled for escalation of the price at 10% from the value fixed by the Reference Court under Ext.A1, which would come to Rs.2,41,710/-.
Thus, we are of the view that the land value has to be re-fixed at Rs.26,58,810/- per Are.
In the result, we allow this appeal by re-fixing the land value at Rs.26,58,810/- per Are.

The appellant will also be entitled to all L.A.A.No.209/2018 :: 4 ::
2025:KER:21099 statutory benefits flowing out of the re-fixation, including proportionate cost in the appeal.

Sd/-
